title: Parasitology and Immunology
mcq: Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is used prophylactically in the case of immunodeficiency diseases, such as hypo- gammaglobulinemia."
Passive transfer is used prophylactically in the case of immunodeficiency diseases, such as hypo- gammaglobulinemia.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are composed of small fragments of disease causing organisms."
Subunit -vaccines are composed of small fragments of disease causing organisms.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a transplant of an organ or tissue between two genetically non-identical members of the same species."
Allograft and allotransplantation An allograft is a transplant of an organ or tissue between two genetically non-identical members of the same species.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a cell that attracts (by chemotaxis), adheres to, engulfs, and ingests foreign bodies."
A phagocyte is a cell that attracts (by chemotaxis), adheres to, engulfs, and ingests foreign bodies.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is an antigen that is recognised by the body as non-self and stimulates an adaptive immune response."
An immunogen is an antigen that is recognised by the body as non-self and stimulates an adaptive immune response.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a biological term that describes a state of having sufficient biological defenses to avoid infection, disease, or other unwanted biological invasion."
Immunity is a biological term that describes a state of having sufficient biological defenses to avoid infection, disease, or other unwanted biological invasion.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a tick borne disease that can cause a skin rash, fever, chills, body aches, and joint pain."
Lyme disease Lyme is a tick borne disease that can cause a skin rash, fever, chills, body aches, and joint pain.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is an antigen that is not yet processed by an APC to smaller parts."
Nativity A native antigen is an antigen that is not yet processed by an APC to smaller parts.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are composed of micro-organisms that have been killed with chemicals and/or heat and are no longer infectious."
Inactivated vaccines are composed of micro-organisms that have been killed with chemicals and/or heat and are no longer infectious.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to nonreplicating microorganisms within the wound, while in infected wounds replicating organisms exist and tissue is injured."
Wound colonisation refers to nonreplicating microorganisms within the wound, while in infected wounds replicating organisms exist and tissue is injured.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is defined by the mixed lymphocyte reaction (MLR) using homozygous stimulating cells for typing."
Class II locus (HLA-D) is defined by the mixed lymphocyte reaction (MLR) using homozygous stimulating cells for typing.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is used to describe antibodies that agglutinate particulate antigens."
The general term agglutinin is used to describe antibodies that agglutinate particulate antigens.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to excessive, undesirable (damaging, discomfort- producing and sometimes fatal) reactions produced by the normal immune system."
Hypersensitivity refers to excessive, undesirable (damaging, discomfort- producing and sometimes fatal) reactions produced by the normal immune system.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the mechanism by which the host eliminates most invading micro-organism by non-specific immunological means."
Innate or non-specific resistance is the mechanism by which the host eliminates most invading micro-organism by non-specific immunological means.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are the microbes, mostly bacteria, that live in and on our bodies with, usually, no harmful effects to us."
Normal flora are the microbes, mostly bacteria, that live in and on our bodies with, usually, no harmful effects to us.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the transfer of active immunity, in the form of readymade antibodies, from one individual to another."
Passive immunity is the transfer of active immunity, in the form of readymade antibodies, from one individual to another.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the strength of the reaction between a single antigenic determinant and a single combining site on the antibody."
Affinity Antibody affinity is the strength of the reaction between a single antigenic determinant and a single combining site on the antibody.
fib: ______ is the colonisation of a host organism by parasite species.
infection
An infection is the colonisation of a host organism by parasite species.
______ is the ability of the host cells to recognise an antigen specifically as a unique molecular entity and distinguish it from another with exquisite precision.
Antigen(ic) specificity
Antigen specificity
Antigen(ic) specificity is the ability of the host cells to recognise an antigen specifically as a unique molecular entity and distinguish it from another with exquisite precision.

______ refers to the ability of an individual antibody combining site to react with more than one antigenic determinant or the ability of a population of antibody molecules to react with more than one antigen.
Cross reactivity

Cross reactivity Cross reactivity refers to the ability of an individual antibody combining site to react with more than one antigenic determinant or the ability of a population of antibody molecules to react with more than one antigen.
______ are a common problem in childhood.
Chronic ear infections
Chronic ear infections Chronic ear infections are a common problem in childhood.
______ is the most obvious mechanical barrier preventing micro- organisms from gaining access to the body.
skin
Surface/Mechanism Barriers The skin is the most obvious mechanical barrier preventing micro- organisms from gaining access to the body.
______ is a powerful enzyme found in mother's milk. f.
Lactoperoxidase
Lactoperoxidase is a powerful enzyme found in mother's milk. f.
______ are those antigens that are presented by MHC I or MHC II molecules on the surface of tumour cells.
Tumour antigens or neoantigens
Tumour antigens Tumour antigens or neoantigens are those antigens that are presented by MHC I or MHC II molecules on the surface of tumour cells.
______ is the body's defence against infectious organisms and other invaders.
immune system
The immune system is the body's defence against infectious organisms and other invaders.
______ is any substance that causes your immune system to produce antibodies against it.
antigen
An antigen is any substance that causes your immune system to produce antibodies against it.
______ is a formidable obstacle insofar as its mucosa secrete hydrochloric acid (0.9 < pH < 3.0, very acidic) and protein-digesting enzymes that kill many pathogens.
stomach
The stomach is a formidable obstacle insofar as its mucosa secrete hydrochloric acid (0.9 < pH < 3.0, very acidic) and protein-digesting enzymes that kill many pathogens.
______ is the case in which organs or tissues are transplanted from a donor to a genetically identical recipient (such as an identical twin).
subset of allografts
A subset of allografts is the case in which organs or tissues are transplanted from a donor to a genetically identical recipient (such as an identical twin).
______ is an important area of study for scientists.
Parasitology and Immunology
Parasitology and Immunology is an important area of study for scientists.
______ is the failure of an organism to recognise its own constituent parts as self, which allows an immune response against its own cells and tissues.
Autoimmunity
Autoimmunity is the failure of an organism to recognise its own constituent parts as self, which allows an immune response against its own cells and tissues.
______ is the only antibody isotype that can pass through the placenta.
IgG
IgG is the only antibody isotype that can pass through the placenta.
______ is the moving of an organ from one body to another or from a donor site on the patient's own body, for the purpose of replacing the recipient's damaged or absent organ.
Organ transplantation
Organ transplantation is the moving of an organ from one body to another or from a donor site on the patient's own body, for the purpose of replacing the recipient's damaged or absent organ.
______ is a serious infection and carries a high complication rate if not treated promptly.
Osteomyelitis
Osteomyelitis is a serious infection and carries a high complication rate if not treated promptly.
